body: The Embraer E175 has become a vital part of the worldwide aviation network, feeding passengers into larger hub-and-spoke systems over 20 years of production. The program launched in 1999, and the first model flew commercially with Air Canada in 2005. According to Key.Aero, over 1,700 examples of the E-Jet family had rolled off the production line as of December last year, including 805 E175s, and the E175 remains in production thanks to strong demand, particularly in the United States, where it holds an approximate 80% share of the regional jet segment.

By modern standards, however, the E175 can be considered loud. According to European Union Aviation Safety Agency type certification documents, an E175 weighing 85,517 pounds at takeoff was measured as producing 84.4 decibels of effective perceived noise during a flyover in 2025, against 83.9 decibels for a CRJ900 of similar weight. The deeper reason is bypass ratio: the E175's GE Aerospace CF34-8E engines, developed in the late nineties, have a bypass ratio of just 5:1 and produce up to 14,500 pounds-force of takeoff thrust. Against International Civil Aviation Organization standards introduced in 2006, which the E175 is said to "meet or surpass," the newer Airbus A220 differs by 18 effective perceived noise decibels.

The A220 comparison shows what newer technology changes. Its Pratt & Whitney PW1500G geared turbofan engines have a bypass ratio of 12:1 and a 73-inch fan, and Airbus says the type's noise footprint is as much as 50% smaller than previous-generation aircraft. A higher-bypass engine accelerates more air around its core than through it, relying less on high-velocity exhaust gases, a significant source of jet noise. Embraer's own successor points the same way: the E190-E2 and E195-E2 use PW1900G engines with a 12:1 bypass ratio, and the future E175-E2's PW1700G is set to offer a 56-inch fan, a 9:1 bypass ratio and 14,000 to 17,000 pounds-force of thrust. Noise still varies with seat position and flight phase, and takeoff, when engines run at high thrust, is when the E175 may appear surprisingly loud for a regional jet.
en.summary: The Embraer E175 still complies with current noise regulations, but its late-1990s CF34-8E engines have a low 5:1 bypass ratio, far below the Airbus A220's 12:1, which helps explain why it sounds loud by modern standards; Embraer's E2 successors use higher-bypass engines to close the gap.
en.title: Why the Embraer E175 sounds loud for a regional jet: its 5:1 bypass ratio

body: E175已成為全球航空網絡的重要一環，20年來為樞紐輻射式航網輸送旅客。E175計畫於1999年啟動，首架飛機於2005年由加拿大航空投入商業飛行；E-Jet家族截至去年12月已生產逾1700架，其中E175占805架，且因需求強勁仍在生產，在美國區域噴射機市場約占80%。

但以現代標準來看，E175可說是偏吵的機型。根據歐洲航空安全局型別認證文件，起飛重量85517磅的E175在2025年飛越噪音測量為84.4分貝有效感覺噪音，相近重量的CRJ900則為83.9分貝。更深層的原因在涵道比：E175搭載的GE航太CF34-8E發動機開發於1990年代末，涵道比僅5:1，起飛推力最高14500磅力；相較之下，A220的PW1500G齒輪渦扇發動機涵道比達12:1、風扇直徑73英寸。涵道比愈高，愈多空氣繞過核心而非穿過核心，也就愈少依賴高速核心排氣產生推力，而核心排氣正是噴射噪音的重要來源。

新機的對照說明了技術世代的差異：空中巴士表示A220的噪音足跡比上一代機型小至多50%，且A220與2006年起實施的國際民航組織標準相差18分貝有效感覺噪音。座位位置與飛行階段也會影響感受，起飛時發動機處於高推力狀態，正是E175顯得格外吵的時候。Embraer自家的後繼機型也朝同一方向發展：E190-E2與E195-E2採用的PW1900G涵道比同為12:1，未來E175-E2的PW1700G風扇直徑56英寸、涵道比9:1、推力14000至17000磅力，可望在噪音表現上超越原版E175。
zh.summary: E175仍符合現行噪音法規，但其1990年代末開發的CF34-8E發動機涵道比僅5:1，遠低於A220的PW1500G的12:1，這正是它在現代標準下顯得較吵的關鍵；E2系列將以更高涵道比的新發動機縮小差距。
zh.title: 為什麼E175聽起來比同級新機吵：關鍵在5:1的低涵道比
